report:
## Conclusion

**The claim is well-supported by high-quality evidence.** Multiple randomized clinical trials and major guideline bodies confirm that tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) initiated in the third trimester significantly reduces mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of hepatitis B in pregnant women with high viral load.

### Key Evidence

1. **Landmark RCT (NEJM 2016):** Pan et al. conducted a multicenter, open-label randomized trial in which TDF was started at 30–32 weeks gestation in highly viremic mothers (HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL). MTCT rates dropped from **18% in the control group to 5% in the TDF group**, alongside standard infant immunoprophylaxis. ([NYU Langone press release](https://nyulangone.org/news/antiviral-treatment-during-pregnancy-reduces-mother-child-transmission-hepatitis-b))

2. **2024 JAMA RCT:** A subsequent randomized trial by Pan et al. confirmed TDF efficacy even in settings without HBIG, reinforcing that third-trimester initiation (from week 28) effectively prevents MTCT. ([JAMA 2024](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2826316))

3. **WHO Recommendation (2020–present):** WHO recommends tenofovir prophylaxis from the 28th week of pregnancy for HBsAg-positive women with HBV DNA ≥200,000 IU/mL. ([WHO](https://www.who.int/teams/global-hiv-hepatitis-and-stis-programmes/hepatitis/prevention/mother-to-child-transmission-of-hepatitis-b))

4. **Systematic reviews** consistently report TDF is both safe and effective for preventing vertical transmission in high-viremia pregnancies. ([Nature Scientific Reports 2017](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-017-04479-x))

### Summary
The evidence is robust: TDF begun in the third trimester (around weeks 28–32) in pregnant women with chronic HBV and high viral load meaningfully reduces MTCT, with favorable safety for mother and infant. This is now standard-of-care per WHO and other guidelines.
